- [RpcModule](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcModule.html)- `server-core`
- Sets of JSON-RPC methods can be organized into “module“s that are in turn registered on the server or,
alternatively, merged with other modules to construct a cohesive API. `RpcModule`
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html)- `server-core`
- Wrapper struct that maintains a subscription “mainly” for testing.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionKey.html)- Key - `server-core`
- Represent a unique subscription entry based on `SubscriptionId``ConnectionId`
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)- Message - `server-core`
- Subscription message.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionSink.html)- Sink - `server-core`
- Represents a single subscription that hasn’t been processed yet.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionState.html)- State - `server-core`
- Helper struct to manage subscriptions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.CallOrSubscription.html)- OrSubscription - `server-core`
- This represent a response to a RPC call
and `Subscribe`calls are handled differently because we want to prevent subscriptions to start before the actual subscription call has been answered.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodCallback.html)- Callback - `server-core`
- Callback wrapper that can be either sync or async.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodKind.html)- Kind - `server-core`
- The kind of the JSON-RPC method call, it can be a subscription, method call or unknown.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodResponseError.html)- Response - Error - `server-core`
- Method response error.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodResult.html)- Result - `server-core`
- Result of a method, either direct value or a future of one.
- [Methods](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)- Error - `server-core`
- The error that can occur when `Methods::call``Methods::subscribe`
- [Notify](https://docs.rs/enum.NotifyMsg.html)- Msg - `server-core`
- A message that that tells whether notification was succesful or not.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/enum.SendTimeoutError.html)- Timeout - Error - `server-core`
- Error that may occur during `crate::server::MethodSink::send_timeout``crate::server::SubscriptionSink::send_timeout`
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/enum.SubscriptionCloseResponse.html)- Close - Response - `server-core`
- Represents what action that will sent when a subscription callback returns.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/enum.SubscriptionMessageInner.html)- Message - Inner - `server-core`
- A complete subscription message or partial subscription message.
- [TrySend](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)- Error - `server-core`
- Error that may occur during `crate::server::MethodSink::try_send``crate::server::SubscriptionSink::try_send`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoResponse.html)- Response - `server-core`
- Something that can be converted into a JSON-RPC method call response.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse.html)- Subscription - Close - Response - `server-core`
- Convert something into a subscription close notification before a subscription is terminated.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [batch_](https://docs.rs/fn.batch_response_error.html)- response_ - error - `server-core`
- Create a JSON-RPC error response.
- [prepare_](https://docs.rs/fn.prepare_error.html)- error - `server-core`

- Max response size.

- [Subscribers](https://docs.rs/type.Subscribers.html)- `server-core`
- Type-alias for subscribers.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/type.SubscriptionMethod.html)- Method - `server-core`

- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/type.SubscriptionPermit.html)- Permit - `server-core`
- Subscription permit.
- [Sync](https://docs.rs/type.SyncMethod.html)- Method - `server-core`
- A `MethodCallback`is an RPC endpoint, callable with a standard JSON-RPC request, implemented as a function pointer to a`Fn`function taking four arguments: the`id`,`params`, a channel the function uses to communicate the result (or error) back to`jsonrpsee`, and the connection ID (useful for the websocket transport).

# jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/index.html

## Expand description

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are available.

- `http-client`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `macros`
- `client-core`
- `client`
- `server-core`
- `server`
- `full`
- `async-client`
- `client-ws-transport`- `ws`transport with TLS.
- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.
- `client-web-transport`- `websys`transport.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_http_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-http-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_http_client/index.html)as http_client;- `jsonrpsee-http-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_ws_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-ws-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_ws_client/index.html)as ws_client;- `jsonrpsee-ws-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_wasm_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-wasm-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_wasm_client/index.html)as wasm_client;- `jsonrpsee-wasm-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_client_transport](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-client-transport/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_client_transport/index.html)as client_transport;- `jsonrpsee-client-transport`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_server](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-server/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_server/index.html)as server;- `server`

- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_proc_macros](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-proc-macros/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_proc_macros/index.html)as proc_macros;- `jsonrpsee-proc-macros`

[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! # Optional features
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! The following features are available.
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! - **`http-client`** - JSON-RPC client functionality over HTTP protocol.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! - **`wasm-client`** - JSON-RPC client functionality over web-sys.
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! - **`ws-client`** - JSON-RPC client functionality over WebSocket protocol.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! - **`macros`** - JSON-RPC API generation convenience by derive macros.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! - **`client-core`** - Enables minimal client features to generate the RPC API without transports.
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! - **`client`** - Enables all client features including transports.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! - **`server-core`** - Enables minimal server features to generate the RPC API without transports.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! - **`server`** - Enables all server features including transports.
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! - **`full`** - Enables all features.
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! - **`async-client`** - Enables the async client without any transport.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! - **`client-ws-transport`** - Enables `ws` transport with TLS.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! - **`client-ws-transport-no-tls`** - Enables `ws` transport without TLS.
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! - **`client-web-transport`** - Enables `websys` transport.
[51](https://docs.rs#51)

# jsonrpsee::async_client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/async_client/index.html

Available on

**crate feature**only.`async-client`## Expand description

Abstract async client.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html)
- Generic asynchronous client.
- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builder for `Client`
- [Ping](https://docs.rs/struct.PingConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for WebSocket ping/pong mechanism and it may be used to disconnect an inactive connection.
- [RpcService](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcService.html)
- RpcService implementation for the async client.

---

- Sink that is used to send back the result to the server for a specific method.

- [prepare_](https://docs.rs/fn.prepare_error.html)- error
- Figure out if this is a sufficiently complete request that we can extract an `Id`

Append a result from an individual method to the batch response.

) -> [MethodSink](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodSink.html)

Create a new `MethodSink` with a limited response size.

Returns whether this channel is closed without needing a context.

Attempts to send out the message immediately and fails if the underlying connection has been closed or if the message buffer is full.

Returns the message if the send fails such that either can be thrown away or re-sent later.

Async send which will wait until there is space in channel buffer or that the subscription is disconnected.

# SubscriptionSink in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/struct.SubscriptionSink.html

`pub struct SubscriptionSink { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

Represents a single subscription that hasn’t been processed yet.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#333)#### pub async fn [send](https://docs.rs#method.send)(
    &self,
    msg: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[SubscriptionMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DisconnectError](https://docs.rs/struct.DisconnectError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#333)

#### pub async fn [send](https://docs.rs#method.send)(
    &self,
    msg: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[SubscriptionMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DisconnectError](https://docs.rs/struct.DisconnectError.html)>

Send out a response on the subscription and wait until there is capacity.

Returns

- `Ok(())`if the message could be sent.
- `Err(unsent_msg)`if the connection or subscription was closed.

[§](https://docs.rs#cancel-safety)Cancel safety

This method is cancel-safe and dropping a future loses its spot in the waiting queue.

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#346-350)#### pub async fn [send_timeout](https://docs.rs#method.send_timeout)(

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#346-350)

Similar to `SubscriptionSink::send` but only waits for a limited time.

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#368)#### pub fn [try_send](https://docs.rs#method.try_send)(

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#368)

#### pub fn [try_send](https://docs.rs#method.try_send)(
    &mut self,
    msg: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[SubscriptionMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [TrySendError](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)>

Attempts to immediately send out the message as JSON string to the subscribers but fails if the channel is full or the connection/subscription is closed

This differs from [ SubscriptionSink::send](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionSink.html#method.send) where it will until there is capacity
in the channel.

# Extensions in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/struct.Extensions.html

`pub struct Extensions { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

A type map of protocol extensions.

`Extensions` can be used by `Request` and `Response` to store
extra data derived from the underlying protocol.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#41)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Extensions)### impl [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#41)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Extensions)

### impl [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

Insert a type into this `Extensions`.

If a extension of this type already existed, it will be returned and replaced with the new one.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
assert!(ext.insert(5i32).is_none());
assert!(ext.insert(4u8).is_none());
assert_eq!(ext.insert(9i32), Some(5i32));
```
Get a reference to a type previously inserted on this `Extensions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
assert!(ext.get::<i32>().is_none());
ext.insert(5i32);
assert_eq!(ext.get::<i32>(), Some(&5i32));
```
Get a mutable reference to a type previously inserted on this `Extensions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
ext.insert(String::from("Hello"));
ext.get_mut::<String>().unwrap().push_str(" World");
assert_eq!(ext.get::<String>().unwrap(), "Hello World");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#119)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert)<T>(&mut self, value: T) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Get a mutable reference to a type, inserting `value` if not already present on this
`Extensions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
*ext.get_or_insert(1i32) += 2;
assert_eq!(*ext.get::<i32>().unwrap(), 3);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#135-138)#### pub fn [get_or_insert_with](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_with)<T, F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#135-138)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_with](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_with)<T, F>(&mut self, f: F) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Get a mutable reference to a type, inserting the value created by `f` if not already present
on this `Extensions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
*ext.get_or_insert_with(|| 1i32) += 2;
assert_eq!(*ext.get::<i32>().unwrap(), 3);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#159)#### pub fn [get_or_insert_default](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_default)<T>(&mut self) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#159)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_default](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_default)<T>(&mut self) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Get a mutable reference to a type, inserting the type’s default value if not already present
on this `Extensions`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-5)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
*ext.get_or_insert_default::<i32>() += 2;
assert_eq!(*ext.get::<i32>().unwrap(), 2);
```
Remove a type from this `Extensions`.

If a extension of this type existed, it will be returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example

```
let mut ext = Extensions::new();
ext.insert(5i32);
assert_eq!(ext.remove::<i32>(), Some(5i32));
assert!(ext.get::<i32>().is_none());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#257)#### pub fn [extend](https://docs.rs#method.extend)(&mut self, other: [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/http/1.4.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/http/extensions.rs.html#257)

#### pub fn [extend](https://docs.rs#method.extend)(&mut self, other: [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html))

Extends `self` with another `Extensions`.

If an instance of a specific type exists in both, the one in `self` is overwritten with the
one from `other`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-10)Example

```
let mut ext_a = Extensions::new();
ext_a.insert(8u8);
ext_a.insert(16u16);
let mut ext_b = Extensions::new();
ext_b.insert(4u8);
ext_b.insert("hello");
ext_a.extend(ext_b);
assert_eq!(ext_a.len(), 3);
assert_eq!(ext_a.get::<u8>(), Some(&4u8));
assert_eq!(ext_a.get::<u16>(), Some(&16u16));
assert_eq!(ext_a.get::<&'static str>().copied(), Some("hello"));
```

# MethodResponse in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/struct.MethodResponse.html

`pub struct MethodResponse { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

Represents a response to a method call.

NOTE: A subscription is also a method call but it’s
possible determine whether a method response
is “subscription” or “ordinary method call”
by calling `MethodResponse::is_subscription`

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#303-307)#### pub async fn [call](https://docs.rs#method.call)<Params, T>(
    &self,
    method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: Params,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#303-307)

#### pub async fn [call](https://docs.rs#method.call)<Params, T>(
    &self,
    method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: Params,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

Helper to call a method on the `RPC module` without having to spin up a server.

The params must be serializable as JSON array, see [ ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html) for further documentation.

Returns the decoded value of the `result field` in JSON-RPC response if successful.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, IntoResponse};
    use jsonrpsee::core::RpcResult;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_method::<RpcResult<u64>, _>("echo_call", |params, _, _| {
        params.one::<u64>().map_err(Into::into)
    }).unwrap();
    let echo: u64 = module.call("echo_call", [1_u64]).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(echo, 1);
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#351-355)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#351-355)

Make a request (JSON-RPC method call or subscription) by using raw JSON.

Returns the raw JSON response to the call and a stream to receive notifications if the call was a subscription.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, SubscriptionMessage};
    use jsonrpsee::types::{response::Success, Response};
    use jsonrpsee::core::to_json_raw_value;
    use futures_util::StreamExt;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_subscription("hi", "hi", "goodbye", |_, pending, _, _| async {
        let sink = pending.accept().await?;
        // see comment above.
        let msg = to_json_raw_value(&"one answer").unwrap();
        sink.send(msg).await?;
        Ok(())
    }).unwrap();
    let (resp, mut stream) = module.raw_json_request(r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hi","id":0}"#, 1).await.unwrap();
    // If the response is an error converting it to `Success` will fail.
    let resp: Success<u64> = serde_json::from_str::<Response<u64>>(resp.get()).unwrap().try_into().unwrap();
    let sub_resp = stream.recv().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        format!(r#"{{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hi","params":{{"subscription":{},"result":"one answer"}}}}"#, resp.result),
        sub_resp.get()
    );
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#442-446)#### pub async fn [subscribe_unbounded](https://docs.rs#method.subscribe_unbounded)(
    &self,
    sub_method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: impl [ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html), [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#442-446)

#### pub async fn [subscribe_unbounded](https://docs.rs#method.subscribe_unbounded)(
    &self,
    sub_method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: impl [ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html), [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

Helper to create a subscription on the `RPC module` without having to spin up a server.

The params must be serializable as JSON array, see [ ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html) for further documentation.

Returns [ Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html) on success which can used to get results from the subscription.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, SubscriptionMessage};
    use jsonrpsee::core::{EmptyServerParams, RpcResult, to_json_raw_value};
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_subscription("hi", "hi", "goodbye", |_, pending, _, _| async move {
        let sink = pending.accept().await?;
        let msg = to_json_raw_value(&"one answer").unwrap();
        sink.send(msg).await?;
        Ok(())
    }).unwrap();
    let mut sub = module.subscribe_unbounded("hi", EmptyServerParams::new()).await.unwrap();
    // In this case we ignore the subscription ID,
    let (sub_resp, _sub_id) = sub.next::<String>().await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(&sub_resp, "one answer");
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#453-458)#### pub async fn [subscribe](https://docs.rs#method.subscribe)(

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html), [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#509)#### pub fn [extensions_mut](https://docs.rs#method.extensions_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#509)

#### pub fn [extensions_mut](https://docs.rs#method.extensions_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

Get a mutable reference to the extensions to add or remove data from the extensions.

This only affects direct calls to the methods and subscriptions and can be used for example to unit test the API without a server.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, IntoResponse, Extensions};
    use jsonrpsee::core::RpcResult;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_method::<RpcResult<u64>, _>("magic_multiply", |params, _, ext| {
        let magic = ext.get::<u64>().copied().unwrap();
        let val = params.one::<u64>()?;
        Ok(val * magic)
    }).unwrap();
    // inject arbitrary data into the extensions.
    module.extensions_mut().insert(33_u64);
    let magic: u64 = module.call("magic_multiply", [1_u64]).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(magic, 33);
}
```

# PendingSubscriptionSink in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/struct.PendingSubscriptionSink.html

`pub struct PendingSubscriptionSink { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

Represents a single subscription that is waiting to be accepted or rejected.

If this is dropped without calling `PendingSubscription::reject` or `PendingSubscriptionSink::accept`
a default error is sent out as response to the subscription call.

Thus, if you want a customized error message then `PendingSubscription::reject` must be called.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#223)#### pub async fn [reject](https://docs.rs#method.reject)(self, err: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[ErrorObject](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-types/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_types/error/struct.ErrorObject.html)<'static>>)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/subscription.rs.html#223)

#### pub async fn [reject](https://docs.rs#method.reject)(self, err: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[ErrorObject](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-types/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_types/error/struct.ErrorObject.html)<'static>>)

Reject the subscription by responding to the subscription method call with
the error message from [ jsonrpsee_types::error::ErrorObject](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-types/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_types/error/struct.ErrorObject.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

If this is used in the async subscription callback the return value is simply ignored because no further notification are propagated once reject has been called.

# RpcModule in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/struct.RpcModule.html

`pub struct RpcModule<Context> { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

Sets of JSON-RPC methods can be organized into “module“s that are in turn registered on the server or,
alternatively, merged with other modules to construct a cohesive API. [ RpcModule](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcModule.html) wraps an additional context
argument that can be used to access data during call execution.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html)+ 'static, Fut:

[Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = R> +

[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)+ 'static, R:

[IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse.html)+

[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html),

Register a new publish/subscribe interface using JSON-RPC notifications.

It implements the [ethereum pubsub specification](https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/rpc/pubsub)
with an option to choose custom subscription ID generation.

Furthermore, it generates the `unsubscribe implementation` where a `bool` is used as
the result to indicate whether the subscription was successfully unsubscribed to or not.
For instance an `unsubscribe call` may fail if a non-existent subscription ID is used in the call.

This method ensures that the `subscription_method_name` and `unsubscription_method_name` are unique.
The `notif_method_name` argument sets the content of the `method` field in the JSON document that
the server sends back to the client. The uniqueness of this value is not machine checked and it’s up to
the user to ensure it is not used in any other [ RpcModule](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcModule.html) used in the server.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `subscription_method_name`- name of the method to call to initiate a subscription
- `notif_method_name`- name of method to be used in the subscription payload (technically a JSON-RPC notification)
- `unsubscription_method`- name of the method to call to terminate a subscription
- `callback`- A callback to invoke on each subscription; it takes three parameters:- `Params`
- `PendingSubscriptionSink`
- Context: Any type that can be embedded into the `RpcModule`

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

An async block which returns something that implements [ crate::server::IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse.html) which
decides what action to take when the subscription ends whether such as to sent out another message
on the subscription stream before closing down it.

NOTE: The return value is ignored if [ PendingSubscriptionSink](https://docs.rs/struct.PendingSubscriptionSink.html) hasn’t been called or is unsuccessful, as the subscription
is not allowed to send out subscription notifications before the actual subscription has been established.

This is implemented for `Result<T, E>` and `()`.

It’s recommended to use `Result` if you want to propagate the error as special error notification
Another option is to implement [ crate::server::IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse.html) if you want customized behaviour.

The error notification has the following format:

```
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "method": "<method>",
 "params": {
   "subscription": "<subscriptionID>",
   "error": <your msg>
   }
 }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use jsonrpsee_core::server::{RpcModule, SubscriptionSink, SubscriptionMessage};
use jsonrpsee_types::ErrorObjectOwned;
let mut ctx = RpcModule::new(99_usize);
ctx.register_subscription("sub", "notif_name", "unsub", |params, pending, ctx, _| async move {
    let x = match params.one::<usize>() {
        Ok(x) => x,
        Err(e) => {
           pending.reject(ErrorObjectOwned::from(e)).await;
           // If the subscription has not been "accepted" then
           // the return value will be "ignored" as it's not
           // allowed to send out any further notifications on
           // on the subscription.
           return Ok(());
        }
    };
    // Mark the subscription is accepted after the params has been parsed successful.
    // This is actually responds the underlying RPC method call and may fail if the
    // connection is closed.
    let sink = pending.accept().await?;
    let sum = x + (*ctx);
    // This will send out an error notification if it fails.
    //
    // If you need some other behavior implement or custom format of the error field
    // you need to manually handle that.
    let msg = serde_json::value::to_raw_value(&sum).unwrap();
    // This fails only if the connection is closed
    sink.send(msg).await?;
    Ok(())
});
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#923-933)#### pub fn [register_subscription_raw](https://docs.rs#method.register_subscription_raw)<R, F>(
    &mut self,
    subscribe_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    notif_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    unsubscribe_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    callback: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&mut [MethodCallback](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodCallback.html), [RegisterMethodError](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/error/enum.RegisterMethodError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#923-933)

#### pub fn [register_subscription_raw](https://docs.rs#method.register_subscription_raw)<R, F>(
    &mut self,
    subscribe_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    notif_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    unsubscribe_method_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    callback: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&mut [MethodCallback](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodCallback.html), [RegisterMethodError](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/error/enum.RegisterMethodError.html)>

Similar to [ RpcModule::register_subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcModule.html#method.register_subscription) but a little lower-level API
where handling the subscription is managed the user i.e, polling the subscription
such as spawning a separate task to do so.

This is more efficient as this doesn’t require cloning the `params` in the subscription
and it won’t send out a close message. Such things are delegated to the user of this API

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use jsonrpsee_core::server::{RpcModule, SubscriptionSink, SubscriptionMessage};
use jsonrpsee_types::ErrorObjectOwned;
let mut ctx = RpcModule::new(99_usize);
ctx.register_subscription_raw("sub", "notif_name", "unsub", |params, pending, ctx, _| {
    // The params are parsed outside the async block below to avoid cloning the bytes.
    let val = match params.one::<usize>() {
        Ok(val) => val,
        Err(e) => {
            // If the subscription has not been "accepted" then
            // the return value will be "ignored" as it's not
            // allowed to send out any further notifications on
            // on the subscription.
            tokio::spawn(pending.reject(ErrorObjectOwned::from(e)));
            return;
        }
    };
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        // Mark the subscription is accepted after the params has been parsed successful.
        // This is actually responds the underlying RPC method call and may fail if the
        // connection is closed.
        let sink = pending.accept().await.unwrap();
        let sum = val + (*ctx);
        let msg = serde_json::value::to_raw_value(&sum).unwrap();
        // This fails only if the connection is closed
        sink.send(msg).await.unwrap();
    });
});
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#303-307)#### pub async fn [call](https://docs.rs#method.call)<Params, T>(
    &self,
    method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: Params,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#303-307)

#### pub async fn [call](https://docs.rs#method.call)<Params, T>(
    &self,
    method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: Params,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

Helper to call a method on the `RPC module` without having to spin up a server.

The params must be serializable as JSON array, see [ ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html) for further documentation.

Returns the decoded value of the `result field` in JSON-RPC response if successful.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, IntoResponse};
    use jsonrpsee::core::RpcResult;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_method::<RpcResult<u64>, _>("echo_call", |params, _, _| {
        params.one::<u64>().map_err(Into::into)
    }).unwrap();
    let echo: u64 = module.call("echo_call", [1_u64]).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(echo, 1);
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#351-355)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#351-355)

Make a request (JSON-RPC method call or subscription) by using raw JSON.

Returns the raw JSON response to the call and a stream to receive notifications if the call was a subscription.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, SubscriptionMessage};
    use jsonrpsee::types::{response::Success, Response};
    use jsonrpsee::core::to_json_raw_value;
    use futures_util::StreamExt;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_subscription("hi", "hi", "goodbye", |_, pending, _, _| async {
        let sink = pending.accept().await?;
        // see comment above.
        let msg = to_json_raw_value(&"one answer").unwrap();
        sink.send(msg).await?;
        Ok(())
    }).unwrap();
    let (resp, mut stream) = module.raw_json_request(r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hi","id":0}"#, 1).await.unwrap();
    // If the response is an error converting it to `Success` will fail.
    let resp: Success<u64> = serde_json::from_str::<Response<u64>>(resp.get()).unwrap().try_into().unwrap();
    let sub_resp = stream.recv().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        format!(r#"{{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hi","params":{{"subscription":{},"result":"one answer"}}}}"#, resp.result),
        sub_resp.get()
    );
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#442-446)#### pub async fn [subscribe_unbounded](https://docs.rs#method.subscribe_unbounded)(
    &self,
    sub_method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: impl [ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html), [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#442-446)

#### pub async fn [subscribe_unbounded](https://docs.rs#method.subscribe_unbounded)(
    &self,
    sub_method: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    params: impl [ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html), [MethodsError](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)>

Helper to create a subscription on the `RPC module` without having to spin up a server.

The params must be serializable as JSON array, see [ ToRpcParams](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/traits/trait.ToRpcParams.html) for further documentation.

Returns [ Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html) on success which can used to get results from the subscription.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, SubscriptionMessage};
    use jsonrpsee::core::{EmptyServerParams, RpcResult, to_json_raw_value};
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_subscription("hi", "hi", "goodbye", |_, pending, _, _| async move {
        let sink = pending.accept().await?;
        let msg = to_json_raw_value(&"one answer").unwrap();
        sink.send(msg).await?;
        Ok(())
    }).unwrap();
    let mut sub = module.subscribe_unbounded("hi", EmptyServerParams::new()).await.unwrap();
    // In this case we ignore the subscription ID,
    let (sub_resp, _sub_id) = sub.next::<String>().await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(&sub_resp, "one answer");
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#509)#### pub fn [extensions_mut](https://docs.rs#method.extensions_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/jsonrpsee_core/server/rpc_module.rs.html#509)

#### pub fn [extensions_mut](https://docs.rs#method.extensions_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)

Get a mutable reference to the extensions to add or remove data from the extensions.

This only affects direct calls to the methods and subscriptions and can be used for example to unit test the API without a server.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    use jsonrpsee::{RpcModule, IntoResponse, Extensions};
    use jsonrpsee::core::RpcResult;
    let mut module = RpcModule::new(());
    module.register_method::<RpcResult<u64>, _>("magic_multiply", |params, _, ext| {
        let magic = ext.get::<u64>().copied().unwrap();
        let val = params.one::<u64>()?;
        Ok(val * magic)
    }).unwrap();
    // inject arbitrary data into the extensions.
    module.extensions_mut().insert(33_u64);
    let magic: u64 = module.call("magic_multiply", [1_u64]).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(magic, 33);
}
```

# CallOrSubscription in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/enum.CallOrSubscription.html

```
pub enum CallOrSubscription {
    Subscription(
```
[MethodResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponse.html)),
    Call([MethodResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponse.html)),
}**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

This represent a response to a RPC call
and `Subscribe` calls are handled differently
because we want to prevent subscriptions to start
before the actual subscription call has been answered.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Subscription)

### Subscription([MethodResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponse.html))

The subscription callback itself sends back the result so it must not be sent back again.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Call)

### Call([MethodResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponse.html))

Treat it as ordinary call.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# SubscriptionCloseResponse in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/enum.SubscriptionCloseResponse.html

```
pub enum SubscriptionCloseResponse {
    None,
    Notif(
```
[SubscriptionMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)),
    NotifErr([SubscriptionError](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/error/struct.SubscriptionError.html)),
}**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

Represents what action that will sent when a subscription callback returns.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.None)

### None

No further message will be sent.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Notif)

### Notif([SubscriptionMessage](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html))

Send a subscription notification.

The subscription notification has the following format:

```
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "method": "<method>",
 "params": {
   "subscription": "<subscriptionID>",
   "result": <your msg>
   }
 }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotifErr)

### NotifErr([SubscriptionError](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-core/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_core/error/struct.SubscriptionError.html))

Send a subscription error notification

The error notification has the following format:

```
{
 "jsonrpc": "2.0",
 "method": "<method>",
 "params": {
   "subscription": "<subscriptionID>",
   "error": <your msg>
   }
 }
}
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

`server-core`## Expand description

Something that can be converted into a JSON-RPC method call response.

If the value couldn’t be serialized/encoded, jsonrpsee will sent out an error
to the client `response could not be serialized`.

# SyncMethod in jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/0.26.0/jsonrpsee/type.SyncMethod.html

`pub type SyncMethod = `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)([Id](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-types/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_types/params/enum.Id.html)<'_>, [Params](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-types/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_types/params/struct.Params.html)<'_>, [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)) -> [MethodResponse](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponse.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)>;**crate feature**only.

`server-core`## Expand description

A `MethodCallback` is an RPC endpoint, callable with a standard JSON-RPC request,
implemented as a function pointer to a `Fn` function taking four arguments:
the `id`, `params`, a channel the function uses to communicate the result (or error)
back to `jsonrpsee`, and the connection ID (useful for the websocket transport).

# jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee/latest/jsonrpsee/

## Expand description

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are available.

- `http-client`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `macros`
- `client-core`
- `client`
- `server-core`
- `server`
- `full`
- `async-client`
- `client-ws-transport`- `ws`transport with TLS.
- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.
- `client-web-transport`- `websys`transport.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_http_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-http-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_http_client/index.html)as http_client;- `jsonrpsee-http-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_ws_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-ws-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_ws_client/index.html)as ws_client;- `jsonrpsee-ws-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_wasm_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-wasm-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_wasm_client/index.html)as wasm_client;- `jsonrpsee-wasm-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_client_transport](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-client-transport/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_client_transport/index.html)as client_transport;- `jsonrpsee-client-transport`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Batch](https://docs.rs/struct.BatchResponse.html)- Response - `server-core`

- A type map of protocol extensions.

- Represents a subscription until it is unsubscribed.

- Represents a response to a method call.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponseFuture.html)- Response - Future - `server-core`
- Future that resolves when the method response has been processed.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodResponseNotifyTx.html)- Response - Notify - Tx - `server-core`
- Sends a message once the method response has been processed.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodSink.html)- Sink - `server-core`
- Sink that is used to send back the result to the server for a specific method.
- [Methods](https://docs.rs/struct.Methods.html)- `server-core`
- Reference-counted, clone-on-write collection of synchronous and asynchronous methods.
- [Pending](https://docs.rs/struct.PendingSubscriptionAcceptError.html)- Subscription - Accept - Error - `server-core`
- The error returned while accepting a subscription.
- [Pending](https://docs.rs/struct.PendingSubscriptionSink.html)- Subscription - Sink - `server-core`
- Represents a single subscription that is waiting to be accepted or rejected.
- [Response](https://docs.rs/struct.ResponsePayload.html)- Payload - `server-core`
- Similar to `jsonrpsee_types::ResponsePayload`
- [RpcModule](https://docs.rs/struct.RpcModule.html)- `server-core`
- Sets of JSON-RPC methods can be organized into “module“s that are in turn registered on the server or,
alternatively, merged with other modules to construct a cohesive API. `RpcModule`
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.Subscription.html)- `server-core`
- Wrapper struct that maintains a subscription “mainly” for testing.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionKey.html)- Key - `server-core`

- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionMessage.html)- Message - `server-core`
- Subscription message.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionSink.html)- Sink - `server-core`
- Represents a single subscription that hasn’t been processed yet.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/struct.SubscriptionState.html)- State - `server-core`
- Helper struct to manage subscriptions.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.CallOrSubscription.html)- OrSubscription - `server-core`
- This represent a response to a RPC call
and `Subscribe`calls are handled differently because we want to prevent subscriptions to start before the actual subscription call has been answered.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodCallback.html)- Callback - `server-core`
- Callback wrapper that can be either sync or async.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodKind.html)- Kind - `server-core`
- The kind of the JSON-RPC method call, it can be a subscription, method call or unknown.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodResponseError.html)- Response - Error - `server-core`
- Method response error.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodResult.html)- Result - `server-core`
- Result of a method, either direct value or a future of one.
- [Methods](https://docs.rs/enum.MethodsError.html)- Error - `server-core`
- The error that can occur when `Methods::call``Methods::subscribe`
- [Notify](https://docs.rs/enum.NotifyMsg.html)- Msg - `server-core`
- A message that that tells whether notification was succesful or not.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/enum.SendTimeoutError.html)- Timeout - Error - `server-core`
- Error that may occur during `crate::server::MethodSink::send_timeout``crate::server::SubscriptionSink::send_timeout`
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/enum.SubscriptionCloseResponse.html)- Close - Response - `server-core`
- Represents what action that will sent when a subscription callback returns.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/enum.SubscriptionMessageInner.html)- Message - Inner - `server-core`
- A complete subscription message or partial subscription message.
- [TrySend](https://docs.rs/enum.TrySendError.html)- Error - `server-core`
- Error that may occur during `crate::server::MethodSink::try_send``crate::server::SubscriptionSink::try_send`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoResponse.html)- Response - `server-core`
- Something that can be converted into a JSON-RPC method call response.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoSubscriptionCloseResponse.html)- Subscription - Close - Response - `server-core`
- Convert something into a subscription close notification before a subscription is terminated.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [batch_](https://docs.rs/fn.batch_response_error.html)- response_ - error - `server-core`
- Create a JSON-RPC error response.
- [prepare_](https://docs.rs/fn.prepare_error.html)- error - `server-core`
- Figure out if this is a sufficiently complete request that we can extract an `Id`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/type.AsyncMethod.html)- Method - `server-core`
- Similar to `SyncMethod`
- [MaxResponse](https://docs.rs/type.MaxResponseSize.html)- Size - `server-core`
- Max response size.
- [RawRpc](https://docs.rs/type.RawRpcResponse.html)- Response - `server-core`
- Raw response from an RPC A tuple containing:
- [Subscribers](https://docs.rs/type.Subscribers.html)- `server-core`
- Type-alias for subscribers.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/type.SubscriptionMethod.html)- Method - `server-core`
- Method callback for subscriptions.
- [Subscription](https://docs.rs/type.SubscriptionPermit.html)- Permit - `server-core`
- Subscription permit.
- [Sync](https://docs.rs/type.SyncMethod.html)- Method - `server-core`
- A `MethodCallback`is an RPC endpoint, callable with a standard JSON-RPC request, implemented as a function pointer to a`Fn`function taking four arguments: the`id`,`params`, a channel the function uses to communicate the result (or error) back to`jsonrpsee`, and the connection ID (useful for the websocket transport).

# jsonrpsee 0.26.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jsonrpsee/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# jsonrpsee

JSON-RPC library designed for async/await in Rust.

Designed to be the successor to [ParityTech's JSONRPC crate](https://github.com/paritytech/jsonrpc/).

## Features

- Client/server HTTP/HTTP2 support
- Client/server WebSocket support
- Client WASM support via web-sys
- Client transport abstraction to provide custom transports
- Middleware

# tokio 1.52.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tokio/^1.42

# Tokio

A runtime for writing reliable, asynchronous, and slim applications with the Rust programming language. It is:

-
**Fast**: Tokio's zero-cost abstractions give you bare-metal performance.
-
**Reliable**: Tokio leverages Rust's ownership, type system, and concurrency model to reduce bugs and ensure thread safety.
-
**Scalable**: Tokio has a minimal footprint, and handles backpressure and cancellation naturally.

[Website](https://tokio.rs) |
[Guides](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial) |
[API Docs](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio) |
[Chat](https://discord.gg/tokio)

## Overview

Tokio is an event-driven, non-blocking I/O platform for writing asynchronous applications with the Rust programming language. At a high level, it provides a few major components:

- A multithreaded, work-stealing based task [scheduler](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/runtime/index.html).
- A reactor backed by the operating system's event queue (epoll, kqueue, IOCP, etc.).
- Asynchronous [TCP and UDP](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/net/index.html)sockets.

These components provide the runtime components necessary for building an asynchronous application.

## Example

A basic TCP echo server with Tokio.

Make sure you enable the full features of the tokio crate on Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.52.3",  = ["full"] }
```
Then, on your main.rs:

```
use TcpListener;
use ;
async
```
More examples can be found [here](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/tree/master/examples). For a larger "real world" example, see the
[mini-redis](https://github.com/tokio-rs/mini-redis/) repository.

To see a list of the available feature flags that can be enabled, check our
[docs](https://docs.rs/tokio/#feature-flags).

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [Guides](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial) or the
[API documentation](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio). If the answer is not there, there is an active community in
the [Tokio Discord server](https://discord.gg/tokio). We would be happy to try to answer your
question. You can also ask your question on [the discussions page](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/discussions).

## Contributing

you! We have a [contributing guide](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/master/docs/contributing/README.md) to help you get involved in the Tokio
project.

## Supported Rust Versions

Tokio will keep a rolling MSRV (minimum supported rust version) policy of **at
least** 6 months. When increasing the MSRV, the new Rust version must have been
released at least six months ago. The current MSRV is 1.71.

Note that the MSRV is not increased automatically, and only as part of a minor release. The MSRV history for past minor releases can be found below:

- 1.48 to now - Rust 1.71
- 1.39 to 1.47 - Rust 1.70
- 1.30 to 1.38 - Rust 1.63
- 1.27 to 1.29 - Rust 1.56
- 1.17 to 1.26 - Rust 1.49
- 1.15 to 1.16 - Rust 1.46
- 1.0 to 1.14 - Rust 1.45

Note that although we try to avoid the situation where a dependency transitively increases the MSRV of Tokio, we do not guarantee that this does not happen. However, every minor release will have some set of versions of dependencies that works with the MSRV of that minor release.

## Release schedule

Tokio doesn't follow a fixed release schedule, but we typically make one minor release each month. We make patch releases for bugfixes as necessary.

## Bug patching policy

For the purposes of making patch releases with bugfixes, we have designated certain minor releases as LTS (long term support) releases. Whenever a bug warrants a patch release with a fix for the bug, it will be backported and released as a new patch release for each LTS minor version. Our current LTS releases are:

- `1.47.x`- LTS release until September 2026. (MSRV 1.70)
- `1.51.x`- LTS release until March 2027. (MSRV 1.71)

Each LTS release will continue to receive backported fixes for at least a year. If you wish to use a fixed minor release in your project, we recommend that you use an LTS release.

To use a fixed minor version, you can specify the version with a tilde. For
example, to specify that you wish to use the newest `1.47.x` patch release, you
can use the following dependency specification:

```
tokio = { version = "~1.47", features = [...] }
```
### Previous LTS releases

- `1.8.x`- LTS release until February 2022.
- `1.14.x`- LTS release until June 2022.
- `1.18.x`- LTS release until June 2023.
- `1.20.x`- LTS release until September 2023.
- `1.25.x`- LTS release until March 2024.
- `1.32.x`- LTS release until September 2024.
- `1.36.x`- LTS release until March 2025.
- `1.38.x`- LTS release until July 2025.
- `1.43.x`- LTS release until March 2026.

# tracing 0.1.44 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tracing/^0.1.34

# tracing

Application-level tracing for Rust.

## Overview

`tracing` is a framework for instrumenting Rust programs to collect
structured, event-based diagnostic information.

In asynchronous systems like Tokio, interpreting traditional log messages can
often be quite challenging. Since individual tasks are multiplexed on the same
thread, associated events and log lines are intermixed making it difficult to
trace the logic flow. `tracing` expands upon logging-style diagnostics by
allowing libraries and applications to record structured events with additional
information about *temporality* and *causality* — unlike a log message, a span
in `tracing` has a beginning and end time, may be entered and exited by the
flow of execution, and may exist within a nested tree of similar spans. In
addition, `tracing` spans are *structured*, with the ability to record typed
data as well as textual messages.

The `tracing` crate provides the APIs necessary for instrumenting libraries
and applications to emit trace data.

*Compiler support:  requires *

`rustc` 1.65+## Usage

(The examples below are borrowed from the `log` crate's yak-shaving
[example](https://docs.rs/log/0.4.10/log/index.html#examples), modified to
idiomatic `tracing`.)

### In Applications

In order to record trace events, executables have to use a `Subscriber`
implementation compatible with `tracing`. A `Subscriber` implements a way of
collecting trace data, such as by logging it to standard output. [ tracing_subscriber](https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/)'s

[provides reasonable defaults. Additionally,](https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/0.3/tracing_subscriber/fmt/index.html)

`fmt` module`tracing-subscriber` is able to consume messages emitted by `log`-instrumented libraries and modules.The simplest way to use a subscriber is to call the `set_global_default` function.

```
use ;
use FmtSubscriber;
```
```
[]
 = "0.1"
 = "0.3.0"
```
This subscriber will be used as the default in all threads for the remainder of the duration
of the program, similar to how loggers work in the `log` crate.

In addition, you can locally override the default subscriber. For example:

```
use ;
use FmtSubscriber;
```
This approach allows trace data to be collected by multiple subscribers within different contexts in the program. Note that the override only applies to the currently executing thread; other threads will not see the change from with_default.

Any trace events generated outside the context of a subscriber will not be collected.

Once a subscriber has been set, instrumentation points may be added to the
executable using the `tracing` crate's macros.

### In Libraries

Libraries should only rely on the `tracing` crate and use the provided macros
and types to collect whatever information might be useful to downstream consumers.

```
use ;
use ;
// the `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute creates and enters a span
// every time the instrumented function is called. The span is named after the
// the function or method. Parameters passed to the function are recorded as fields.
```
```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
Note: Libraries should *NOT* call `set_global_default()`, as this will cause
conflicts when executables try to set the default later.

### In Asynchronous Code

If you are instrumenting code that make use of
[ std::future::Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/future/trait.Future.html)
or async/await, avoid using the

`Span::enter` method. The following example
*will not*work:

```
async
```
```
async
```
The span guard `_s` will not exit until the future generated by the `async` block is complete.
Since futures and spans can be entered and exited *multiple* times without them completing,
the span remains entered for as long as the future exists, rather than being entered only when
it is polled, leading to very confusing and incorrect output.
For more details, see [the documentation on closing spans](https://tracing.rs/tracing/span/index.html#closing-spans).

There are two ways to instrument asynchronous code. The first is through the
[ Future::instrument](https://docs.rs/tracing/latest/tracing/trait.Instrument.html#method.instrument) combinator:

```
use Instrument;
let my_future = async ;
my_future
    .instrument
    .await
```
`Future::instrument` attaches a span to the future, ensuring that the span's lifetime
is as long as the future's.

The second, and preferred, option is through the
[ #[instrument]](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/tracing/attr.instrument.html)
attribute:

```
use ;
use ;
use io;
async
```
Under the hood, the `#[instrument]` macro performs the same explicit span
attachment that `Future::instrument` does.

### Concepts

This crate provides macros for creating `Span`s and `Event`s, which represent
periods of time and momentary events within the execution of a program,
respectively.

As a rule of thumb, *spans* should be used to represent discrete units of work
(e.g., a given request's lifetime in a server) or periods of time spent in a
given context (e.g., time spent interacting with an instance of an external
system, such as a database). In contrast, *events* should be used to represent
points in time within a span — a request returned with a given status code,
*n* new items were taken from a queue, and so on.

`Span`s are constructed using the `span!` macro, and then *entered*
to indicate that some code takes place within the context of that `Span`:

```
use ;
// Construct a new span named "my span".
let mut span = span!;
span.in_scope;
// Dropping the span will close it, indicating that it has ended.
```
The [ #[instrument]](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/tracing/attr.instrument.html) attribute macro
can reduce some of this boilerplate:

```
use ;
```
The `Event` type represent an event that occurs instantaneously, and is
essentially a `Span` that cannot be entered. They are created using the `event!`
macro:

```
use ;
event!;
```
Users of the [ log](https://docs.rs/log/0.4.6/log/) crate should note that

`tracing` exposes a set of macros for
creating `Event`s (`trace!`, `debug!`, `info!`, `warn!`, and `error!`) which may
be invoked with the same syntax as the similarly-named macros from the `log`
crate. Often, the process of converting a project to use `tracing` can begin
with a simple drop-in replacement.## Supported Rust Versions

Tracing is built against the latest stable release. The minimum supported version is 1.42. The current Tracing version is not guaranteed to build on Rust versions earlier than the minimum supported version.

Tracing follows the same compiler support policies as the rest of the Tokio project. The current stable Rust compiler and the three most recent minor versions before it will always be supported. For example, if the current stable compiler version is 1.45, the minimum supported version will not be increased past 1.42, three minor versions prior. Increasing the minimum supported compiler version is not considered a semver breaking change as long as doing so complies with this policy.

## Ecosystem

### Related Crates

In addition to `tracing` and `tracing-core`, the [ tokio-rs/tracing](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing) repository
contains several additional crates designed to be used with the

`tracing` ecosystem.
This includes a collection of `Subscriber` implementations, as well as utility
and adapter crates to assist in writing `Subscriber`s and instrumenting
applications.In particular, the following crates are likely to be of interest:

- `tracing-futures`- `futures`crate, allowing spans to be attached to- `Future`s,- `Stream`s, and- `Executor`s.
- `tracing-subscriber`- `Subscriber`implementations and utilities for working with- `Subscriber`s. This includes a- `FmtSubscriber`- `FmtSubscriber`for logging formatted trace data to stdout, with similar filtering and formatting to the- `env_logger`
- `tracing-log`- `log`- `tracing`- `Event`s within the trace tree. This is useful when a project using- `tracing`have dependencies which use- `log`. Note that if you're using- `tracing-subscriber`'s- `FmtSubscriber`, you don't need to depend on- `tracing-log`directly.

Additionally, there are also several third-party crates which are not
maintained by the `tokio` project. These include:

- `tracing-timing`- `tracing`. It provides a subscriber that records the time elapsed between pairs of- `tracing`events and generates histograms.
- `tracing-opentelemetry`- [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/)-compatible distributed tracing systems.
- `tracing-honeycomb`- [honeycomb.io](https://www.honeycomb.io/). Backed by- `tracing-distributed`
- `tracing-distributed`
- `tracing-actix`- `tracing`integration for the- `actix`actor framework.
- `axum-insights`- `tracing`integration and Application insights export for the- `axum`web framework.
- `tracing-gelf`
- `tracing-coz`- [coz](https://github.com/plasma-umass/coz)causal profiler (Linux-only).
- `test-log`- `tracing`for tests, based on environment variables with an- `env_logger`compatible syntax.
- `tracing-unwrap`- `Result`or- `Option`types to a- `Subscriber`.
- `diesel-tracing`- `diesel`
- `tracing-tracy`- [Tracy](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy)profiles in instrumented applications.
- `tracing-elastic-apm`- [Elastic APM](https://www.elastic.co/apm).
- `tracing-etw`- [ETW](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)events.
- `tracing-fluent-assertions`- `tracing`spans.
- `sentry-tracing`- [Sentry](https://sentry.io/welcome/).
- `tracing-loki`- [Grafana Loki](https://grafana.com/oss/loki/).
- `tracing-logfmt`
- `json-subscriber`- `FmtSubscriber`

If you're the maintainer of a `tracing` ecosystem crate not listed above,
please let us know! We'd love to add your project to the list!

**Note:** that some of the ecosystem crates are currently unreleased and
undergoing active development. They may be less stable than `tracing` and
`tracing-core`.

## Supported Rust Versions

Tracing is built against the latest stable release. The minimum supported version is 1.65. The current Tracing version is not guaranteed to build on Rust versions earlier than the minimum supported version.

Tracing follows the same compiler support policies as the rest of the Tokio project. The current stable Rust compiler and the three most recent minor versions before it will always be supported. For example, if the current stable compiler version is 1.69, the minimum supported version will not be increased past 1.66, three minor versions prior. Increasing the minimum supported compiler version is not considered a semver breaking change as long as doing so complies with this policy.

# jsonrpsee 0.25.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jsonrpsee/0.25.1

# jsonrpsee

JSON-RPC library designed for async/await in Rust.

Designed to be the successor to [ParityTech's JSONRPC crate](https://github.com/paritytech/jsonrpc/).

## Features

- Client/server HTTP/HTTP2 support
- Client/server WebSocket support
- Client WASM support via web-sys
- Client transport abstraction to provide custom transports
- Middleware

## Documentation

## Examples

- [HTTP](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/http.rs)
- [WebSocket](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/ws.rs)
- [WebSocket pubsub](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/ws_pubsub_broadcast.rs)
- [API generation with proc macro](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/proc_macro.rs)
- [CORS server](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/cors_server.rs)
- [Core client](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/core_client.rs)
- [HTTP proxy middleware](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/http_proxy_middleware.rs)
- [jsonrpsee as service](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/jsonrpsee_as_service.rs)
- [low level API](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/jsonrpsee_server_low_level_api.rs)
- [Websocket served over dual-stack (v4/v6) sockets](https://docs.rs/examples/examples/ws_dual_stack.rs)

See [this directory](https://docs.rs/examples/examples) for more examples

## Roadmap

See [our tracking milestone](https://github.com/paritytech/jsonrpsee/milestone/2) for the upcoming stable v1.0 release.

## Users

If your project uses `jsonrpsee` we would like to know. Please open a pull request and add your project to the list below:

- [parity bridges common](https://github.com/paritytech/parity-bridges-common)
- [remote externalities](https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/tree/master/utils/frame/remote-externalities)
- [polkadot-sdk](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk)
- [substrate-api-client](https://github.com/scs/substrate-api-client)
- [subwasm](https://github.com/chevdor/subwasm)
- [subway](https://github.com/AcalaNetwork/subway)
- [subxt](https://github.com/paritytech/subxt)
- [Trin](https://github.com/ethereum/trin)
- [Uptest](https://github.com/uptest-sc/uptest)
- [zkSync Era](https://github.com/matter-labs/zksync-era)
- [Forest](https://github.com/ChainSafe/forest)

## Benchmarks

Daily benchmarks for jsonrpsee can be found:

- Gitlab machine: [https://paritytech.github.io/jsonrpsee/bench/dev2](https://paritytech.github.io/jsonrpsee/bench/dev2)

# jsonrpsee 0.24.9 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jsonrpsee/0.24.9

# jsonrpsee

JSON-RPC library designed for async/await in Rust.

Designed to be the successor to [ParityTech's JSONRPC crate](https://github.com/paritytech/jsonrpc/).

## Features

# jsonrpsee 0.16.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jsonrpsee/0.16.3

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

# Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are available.

- `http-client`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `macros`
- `client-core`
- `client`
- `server-core`
- `server`
- `full`
- `async-client`
- `client-ws-transport`- `ws`transport with TLS.
- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.
- `client-web-transport`- `websys`transport.

---

# jsonrpsee 0.15.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/jsonrpsee/0.15.1

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

# Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are avaliable.

- `http-client`
- `http-server`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `ws-server`
- `macros`
- `client`- `http-client`and- `ws-client`features.
- `server`- `http-server`and- `ws-server`features.

- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.

# jsonrpsee 0.15.0 - Docs.rs

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

# Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are avaliable.

- `http-client`
- `http-server`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `ws-server`
- `macros`
- `client`- `http-client`and- `ws-client`features.
- `server`- `http-server`and- `ws-server`features.
- `full`- `client`,- `server`and- `macros`features.
- `async-client`
- `client-ws-transport`- `ws`transport with TLS.
- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.

# jsonrpsee - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee

## Expand description

jsonrpsee wrapper crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

The `jsonrpsee` crate composes JSON-RPC functionality behind optional feature
flags to provide for client and server communication over specific protocols.
There are no default features, all functionality must be opted in to accordingly.
The following features are available.

- `http-client`
- `wasm-client`
- `ws-client`
- `macros`
- `client-core`
- `client`
- `server-core`
- `server`
- `full`
- `async-client`
- `client-ws-transport`- `ws`transport with TLS.
- `client-ws-transport-no-tls`- `ws`transport without TLS.
- `client-web-transport`- `websys`transport.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_http_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-http-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_http_client/index.html)as http_client;- `jsonrpsee-http-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_ws_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-ws-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_ws_client/index.html)as ws_client;- `jsonrpsee-ws-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_wasm_client](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-wasm-client/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_wasm_client/index.html)as wasm_client;- `jsonrpsee-wasm-client`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_client_transport](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-client-transport/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_client_transport/index.html)as client_transport;- `jsonrpsee-client-transport`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_server](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-server/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_server/index.html)as server;- `server`
- `pub use`- [tokio](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/index.html);- `server`
- `pub use`- [jsonrpsee_proc_macros](https://docs.rs/jsonrpsee-proc-macros/0.26.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/jsonrpsee_proc_macros/index.html)as proc_macros;- `jsonrpsee-proc-macros`
- `pub use`- [tracing](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tracing/index.html);- `jsonrpsee-proc-macros`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Abstract async client.
- [helpers](https://docs.rs/helpers/index.html)- `server-core`
- Helpers.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)
